title: Seamless Private Upgrade Planner with Orchestrated Schema & Config Migrations
creator: Carlos Mendes
description:
Goal: Build an orchestration-first upgrade planner and executor for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) that sequences schema migrations, config transforms, agent upgrades, and helm/manifest updates across clusters with LTS-aware gating and automated rollback semantics. The tool should generate an idempotent, auditable 'upgrade plan' that the private delivery agent executes, with built-in pre-checks, canary rollouts, and automated failure mitigation.

Scope:
- Planner: computes dependency graph between components (database schemas, platform API, private agent, nodes, helm charts) and emits ordered steps and checkpoints.
- Migration runner: executes DB migrations (Postgres/Timescale), supports transactional/online migrations where possible, and provides compensating steps for irreversible changes.
- Rollout gates: LTS channel enforcement, canary percentage scheduling, health-check metric gates (latency, error-rate, JVM/OOM signals), and manual approval hooks.
- Upgrade executor: agent-based orchestration that applies the plan per-cluster, tracks progress, streams logs back to Console, and can trigger automated rollback on gate failures.
- Safety features: snapshot/backup hooks, pre-flight compatibility checks (binary + schema compatibility matrix), agent connectivity checks, KMS key access validation, and a dead-letter path for failed migrations.
- Observability: per-step metrics, SLO check results, audit log entries, drift detection for post-upgrade validation, and links to artifacts for debugging.
- UX/Integration: plan preview in Console (read-only for on-prem customers by default), one-click dry-run, and GitHub/Confluence links stored with each run for postmortems.

Design notes / constraints:
- Must support customers with air-gapped clusters; planner must be able to export a signed plan bundle that an offline agent can consume.
- Migrations must be idempotent; runner will record applied step IDs in an upgrade_state table for each cluster.
- Support multi-tenant private installs where platform control plane upgrades can be staggered by namespace/pool.
- LTS channels: planner needs awareness of LTS vs non-LTS build compatibility matrix to avoid downgrades or incompatible binary/schema combos.

Acceptance criteria (done when):
- Planner can generate a complete plan for a representative 3-node on-prem deployment including DB, agent, and helm chart changes.
- Migration runner successfully applies and rolls back a sample irreversible migration in a staging cluster (automation test).
- Console displays plan preview with step-level annotations and a dry-run mode that simulates execution without mutating state.
- Canary gating works end-to-end: deploy 10% canary, observe metric evaluation, and automatically proceed or rollback based on thresholds.
- Exportable signed plan bundle can be applied by an offline agent and produces identical step ordering to an online run.
- All upgrade runs produce audit records with plan hash, operator, start/end timestamps, and step results visible in Console and in the upgrade_state table.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Full transactional DB migrations limit some schema changes; we will provide transform profiles and recommend background/online migration patterns for large tables.
- Air-gapped export increases complexity of signature/key management; we will rely on customer-provided KMS or signed tokens with expiry.
- Aggressive automation could lead to customer-visible regressions; default to manual approval for high-risk steps and make automatic rollback conservative by default.

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Prototype planner PoC that ingests a simple manifest and outputs an ordered step plan (owner: Sofia).
2) Design the upgrade_state schema and migration step idempotency model (owner: DB eng).
3) Wire a minimal runner that can execute plan steps in a staging cluster and stream logs to a temporary Console UI.
4) Create an RFC describing plan bundle format for air-gapped customers and sign-off checklist for security.

Links to artifacts: 
- RFC (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Private+Upgrade+Planner+RFC
- PoC repo (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrade-planner/pulls/12
- Design diagram (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-upgrade-planner-diagrams

Notes for reviewers: include DB and infra on-call when reviewing migrations strategy. Prioritize making pre-flight checks fast and non-blocking for large clusters.
comments: 2026-02-11 | Sofia Nguyen: Kickoff meeting done. Agreed on step-idempotency and upgrade_state recording as core invariant. Action: prototype planner by Feb 24.

2026-02-18 | Carlos Mendes: Spike findings - two patterns for online DB migration (ghost copies vs background transforms). Ghost copy approach safe but requires double writes during transition. Documented in RFC link.

2026-02-25 | Priya Shah (DB Eng): Implemented initial upgrade_state schema stub; added indexes and cluster_id partitioning. Pushed draft schema to PoC repo. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrade-planner/pull/8
2026-03-03 | Security (review): Raised concern about signing plan bundles for air-gapped installs. Need KMS integration or customer-provided public key. Added security checklist to RFC.
2026-03-07 | Sofia Nguyen: Canary gating prototype wired to Prometheus-based SLO checks. Observed flakiness in one health check — added retry/backoff and extended evaluation window to 5m.

2026-03-10 | Product (Ethan Martinez): Reviewed acceptance criteria; requested that dry-run include a detailed report of potential incompatible steps and suggested a user-facing mitigation guide in Console.
